interconnectors.name: Eastern Green Link 1 (Torness to Hawthorn Pit)

ai_summary:
Scotland’s power system is currently operating under exceptional renewable saturation, anchored by wind generation reaching 4.4 GW. This high volume of clean generation has driven regional carbon intensity down to an impressive 32 gCO2/kWh, demonstrating Scotland’s ongoing role as the primary decarbonization engine for the wider British electricity network.

Despite this operational success, systemic transmission constraints continue to impede total asset efficiency. Wasted energy stands at 221.1 MWh, driven by localized curtailment across critical export boundaries, notably the B6 corridor into England. With generation exceeding both regional demand and the physical transfer limits of existing infrastructure, system operators must constrain zero-marginal-cost turbines to maintain frequency stability and keep lines within thermal limits.

This structural curtailment underscores the urgency of accelerated transmission reinforcements, such as the Eastern Green Link subsea cables, alongside regional battery installations and long-duration storage assets. Until network transfer capacities expand to match Scotland’s growing renewable buildout, operators must rely on dynamic line ratings and commercial demand response to monetize stranded output. Fully integrating these high-yield wind events remains essential to lowering consumer balancing costs and sustaining long-term grid decarbonization.
